metadata.notes: agent_supports: yes (FailoverReason.rate_limit/billing, backoff + failover, terminal 'Billing or credits exhausted' result); daemon_capability: incapable (the walled turn is never persisted -- no assistant row, no finish_reason='stop', no ended_at, and the messages table has no error column -- so the session sticks in working); driver_capability: gap:429-mock

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: incapable; driver_capability: gap:429-mock
route: frozen

## What the scenario asserts

State-only: the agent is `working`, hits its token/cost budget, emits a turn-end
signal, the session goes `working -> ready`, and subsequent prompts keep it
`ready` until the budget resets (final state `ready`, at least 1 turn). No quota
METRIC is asserted -- the acceptance_criteria are a lifecycle arc.

## agent_supports: yes

Hermes has a first-class quota/billing wall, not an accidental one.
`agent/error_classifier.py` defines `FailoverReason.rate_limit` ("429 or
quota-based throttling"), `billing` ("402 or confirmed credit exhaustion") and
`upstream_rate_limit`. `agent/conversation_loop.py` consumes them: adaptive
backoff (`adaptive_rate_limit_backoff`, conversation_loop.py:77), credential
rotation / provider fallback (conversation_loop.py:4005-4063, the user-visible
"Rate limited -- switching to fallback provider..." at :4042 and "Billing or
credits exhausted -- switching to fallback provider..." at :4035), a Nous-Portal
guard that records the reset window (`agent/nous_rate_guard.py` ->
`$HERMES_HOME/rate_limits/nous.json`), and -- when retries and failover are
exhausted -- a terminal turn result at conversation_loop.py:4959-5010 carrying
`completed: False`, `failed: True`, `failure_reason: "rate_limit"|"billing"`,
and `final_response = "Billing or credits exhausted: ..."`. The REPL renders it
plus a durable billing CTA panel (cli.py:12975, :13063-13110). The behavior is
real, deterministic under a stubbed provider, and user-visible. So `yes`.

## daemon_capability: incapable

`Source` is `agent.ProcessOwnedStore` over `$HERMES_HOME/state.db`
(core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/agent.go:37-43) -- Hermes writes no
transcript file, so the store is the whole observable surface. The adapter has
exactly TWO ways to settle a turn:

1. `messages.finish_reason = 'stop'` on the newest assistant row --
   `Watcher.turnIsDone` (watcher.go:426-436) sets `Terminal` on the activity
   event, and `Parser.ParseLine` maps that row to `turn_done` (parser.go:93-95).
2. `sessions.ended_at` going non-NULL -- the `justEnded` branch
   (watcher.go:408-418) emits one final terminal event.

The adapter deliberately carries no idle-flush seam because finish_reason is
supposed to be an explicit boundary (parser.go:23-25).

**On a quota wall Hermes writes neither.**

- No assistant row. The terminal failure path returns at
  conversation_loop.py:4959-5010 after calling
  `agent._persist_session(messages, conversation_history)` (:4959). Nothing in
  the whole retry/failover region appends an assistant message to that list --
  `grep -n "messages.append" agent/conversation_loop.py` has NO hit between
  lines 3800 and 5100. `_persist_session` (run_agent.py:1772-1805) delegates to
  `_flush_messages_to_session_db`, whose `append_message` call takes
  `finish_reason=msg.get("finish_reason")` straight off each in-memory message
  (run_agent.py:2079-2095) -- so a row that was never appended is never written.
  `_drop_trailing_empty_response_scaffolding` (run_agent.py:1807+) goes further
  and actively STRIPS the retry/failure sentinels before the write.
- No session close. The REPL survives the failed turn (it returns to the prompt
  and prints the error), so `ended_at` stays NULL and the `justEnded` branch
  never fires.
- No error field to read instead. The `messages` table has no error column at
  all (hermes_state.py:1182-1204: role/content/tool_calls/tool_call_id/
  tool_name/finish_reason/display_kind/... and nothing else), unlike opencode's
  `message.data.error`, which is exactly what irrlicht's opencode watcher was
  taught to treat as terminal in #493. `sessions.end_reason`
  (hermes_state.py:1147) only ever holds session-close reasons -- 'compression',
  'branched', 'agent_close', 'tui_shutdown', 'ws_orphan_reap' -- never a quota
  reason. And `sessions.billing_mode`, which does exist on the row, is a PRICING
  route label ('subscription_included' / 'official_models_api' /
  'official_docs_snapshot' / 'unknown', agent/usage_pricing.py:913-939), not a
  quota state; it never flips on exhaustion.
- The error is display-only. cli.py:12975 turns `result["error"]` into
  "Error: ..." for the panel and cli.py:13090 adds the billing CTA; neither
  persists anything. The only two `conversation_history.append` sites in cli.py
  (:11073, :12569) are user-side.

Consequence in the daemon: after the wall the newest row for the session is the
user prompt (or a tool result), `message_count` does not grow, so
`reconcile` emits no further activity event at all (watcher.go:408-418); and if
a later scan did emit one, `turnIsDone` is false so `Terminal` stays false. The
metrics fold leaves `LastEventType = "user_message"` (metrics.go:135 <-
parser.go:79), `IsAgentDone()` is false, and the classifier falls to its last
rung `transcript_activity -> working`
(core/application/services/state_classifier.go:204-212). There is no wall-clock
or idle rule anywhere in `stateRules` (state_classifier.go:100-212) and no
idle-to-ready sweeper in services (the only sweeps are dead-PID / superseded
presession in pid_manager.go). **The session sticks in `working` for as long as
the REPL lives**, so both the `working -> ready` transition and the "subsequent
prompts stay ready" criterion are unobservable.

That is `incapable`, not `bug`: the daemon is not mis-handling a trace, Hermes
persists no trace of the failed turn into the source the daemon tails. The one
durable quota artifact Hermes does write --
`$HERMES_HOME/rate_limits/nous.json` (agent/nous_rate_guard.py:29-36,106-122) --
sits OUTSIDE the store (and outside the 'store' permission's declared Touches,
agent.go:44-59), is Nous-Portal-only, and is a reset-time marker rather than a
turn boundary. Teaching the adapter to read it could someday give Hermes a
codex-style quota METRIC; it still would not produce the state arc this scenario
asserts.

## driver_capability: gap:429-mock

Elicitation is wireable in principle -- Hermes honors `OPENAI_BASE_URL` /
`OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment or `$HERMES_HOME/.env`
(hermes_cli/config.py:264, hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py:1808), so the existing
`tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-429` (built for the opencode
sibling: 200 + finish_reason stop on request 1, an insufficient_quota error
after) could serve the 200-then-wall pair against an OpenAI-compatible provider
entry in `config.yaml`. What is missing is the harness: the only quota recorder,
`tools/onboarding-factory/recording/record-token-quota-exhausted.sh`, is
hard-wired to `claude --bare` + `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and
`replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh` has no mock-launch primitive
(`DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"`), so a gemini-style teardown
recipe (`keys` Escape / `sigkill` / `exit_clean`) would additionally land on
stubbed arms. Primary label `gap:429-mock`, matching the codex and mistral-vibe
siblings. Moot for routing: even a perfect harness cannot make the arc
observable. A driver-visible symptom of the same missing signal: hermes'
`wait_turn` polls `messages ... finish_reason='stop'`, so it would spin to its
deadline on the walled turn.

## Route

`agent=yes` + `daemon=incapable` -> **frozen**. This unblocks only if upstream
Hermes persists the walled turn (an assistant/system row carrying a terminal
finish_reason, or ended_at/end_reason set on the quota wall) AND the adapter
learns to settle on it -- an upstream + adapter change, not a tooling task. The
same shape as the mistral-vibe sibling, and the mirror image of opencode, whose
store DOES carry `message.data.error` and whose watcher settles on it.
caveats: Decisive claim is a code read of Hermes 0.19.0, not a live run (assess spends no CLI tokens): no `messages.append` exists anywhere in conversation_loop.py:3800-5100, and _flush_messages_to_session_db (run_agent.py:2079-2095) writes rows only from that in-memory list -- so no assistant row and no finish_reason='stop' can reach the store on a quota wall.

One-shot nuance, and why it does NOT unfreeze the cell: `hermes -z` exits after the failed turn, the session then gets ended_at/end_reason, and the watcher's justEnded branch (watcher.go:408-418) emits a terminal event -> ready. That arc is teardown, byte-identical to a normal one-shot end, and cannot satisfy the 'subsequent user prompts stay ready' criterion (there is no subsequent prompt).

Provider failover can mask the wall entirely: with a fallback provider configured, Hermes switches (conversation_loop.py:4035-4063) and the turn completes normally with finish_reason='stop' -- the recording would then show an ordinary basic-turn arc, not quota exhaustion. A recording harness would have to 429 every configured provider.

sessions.billing_mode / estimated_cost_usd are pricing-route labels (agent/usage_pricing.py:913-939), not quota state; the adapter deliberately re-prices via capacity instead of trusting them (metrics.go:155-163). Neither carries an exhaustion signal.

$HERMES_HOME/rate_limits/nous.json (agent/nous_rate_guard.py) is the only durable quota artifact Hermes writes. It is outside the tailed store and outside the 'store' permission's Touches, is Nous-Portal-only, and is a reset-time marker -- a possible future quota METRIC, never the lifecycle arc this scenario asserts.

Hermes retries and backs off hard before giving up (adaptive_rate_limit_backoff, nous_rate_guard), so the stuck-in-working stretch begins well before the wall is final. That is a duration nuance, not the blocker.

Driver secondary gaps beyond the mock: DRIVE_ELICITS is 'send slash sleep wait_turn', so keys/sigkill/exit_clean are stubbed; and wait_turn polls for finish_reason='stop', which the walled turn never writes, so it would time out.

sources.note: Terminal quota/billing failure: _persist_session(messages, conversation_history) then return {completed:False, failed:True, failure_reason:'rate_limit'|'billing', final_response:'Billing or credits exhausted: ...'}. No assistant message is appended -- grep shows no messages.append between lines 3800 and 5100.
FailoverReason taxonomy: rate_limit ('429 or quota-based throttling'), billing ('402 or confirmed credit exhaustion'), upstream_rate_limit. Grounds agent_supports=yes.

The DB write is driven entirely by the in-memory messages list, taking finish_reason per message; _drop_trailing_empty_response_scaffolding strips retry/failure sentinels before the write. A row never appended is never persisted.

Schema: messages has no error column (only finish_reason as a failure-adjacent field); sessions.end_reason holds close reasons only ('compression','branched','agent_close','tui_shutdown','ws_orphan_reap' -- hermes_state.py:4140,4305). No quota state anywhere in the store.
billing_mode is a pricing-route label ('subscription_included','official_models_api','official_docs_snapshot','unknown'), never an exhaustion flag.

The quota failure is display-only: result['error'] becomes 'Error: ...' in a Rich panel plus a billing CTA. The two conversation_history.append sites (cli.py:11073,12569) are user-side, so nothing persists the failure.
The only durable quota artifact: $HERMES_HOME/rate_limits/nous.json (reset-time marker, Nous Portal only) -- outside state.db, outside the adapter's Source and its 'store' permission.

The adapter's only two settle paths: turnIsDone requires role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop' on the newest row; justEnded requires ended_at to go non-NULL. An activity event is emitted only when message_count grows or the session just ended.
finish_reason is the load-bearing turn boundary and the adapter deliberately has NO idle-flush seam; a user row maps to user_message, so LastEventType stays user_message after the wall.

The stateRules ladder has no wall-clock/idle rule; with IsAgentDone false the last rung transcript_activity holds the session in working. No idle-to-ready sweeper exists in services (pid_manager.go sweeps only dead PIDs).

Source = ProcessOwnedStore over $HERMES_HOME/state.db; the 'store' observe permission's Touches is that file only -- so a signal written elsewhere (rate_limits/nous.json, stderr, the TUI) is out of the daemon's reach by construction.

OPENAI_BASE_URL / OPENAI_API_KEY are honored from env or $HERMES_HOME/.env, so tools/onboarding-factory/recording/mock-openai-429 could in principle be pointed at -- the gap is the missing recorder/driver wiring, not the mock.
The only quota recorder is hard-wired to claude --bare + ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; the hermes driver has DRIVE_ELICITS='send slash sleep wait_turn' and no mock-launch primitive -> gap:429-mock.

Precedent for both sides: vibe is frozen for the identical reason (the 429 turn is never persisted); opencode's store DOES carry message.data.error and its watcher settles on it (#493) -- which is exactly the field hermes' schema lacks.

recipe.notes: Not recordable (route: frozen; daemon=incapable). Hermes DOES hit the quota wall (FailoverReason.rate_limit/billing -> the terminal failure result at conversation_loop.py:4959-5010), but nothing about it reaches $HERMES_HOME/state.db: no assistant row is appended in the failure path (no messages.append in conversation_loop.py:3800-5100), _flush_messages_to_session_db writes only from that list (run_agent.py:2079-2095), the REPL survives so ended_at stays NULL, and the messages table has no error column (hermes_state.py:1182-1204). With neither finish_reason='stop' nor ended_at, watcher.turnIsDone/justEnded never fire (watcher.go:408-418,426-436), LastEventType stays user_message, and the classifier's last rung holds the session in working (state_classifier.go:204-212) -- there is no idle->ready path. Secondary: no hermes 429 harness (record-token-quota-exhausted.sh is claude-only) and the driver has no mock-launch primitive, hence gap:429-mock; the existing mock-openai-429 plus OPENAI_BASE_URL would cover elicitation once wired. Becomes recordable only if upstream Hermes persists the walled turn AND the adapter settles on it. See assessment.body.
